text.p: Following are the top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Urging ASEAN to stay strong and united, Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad lambasts Western countries for criticising ASEAN's expansion to embrace all Southeast Asian states.
- Thirty-seven-year-old woman and 13-year-old son charged in court with hurting Indonesian maid last month.
- By June next year, retailers will have to be licensed to sell cigarettes, move aimed at keeping young people from smoking.

- Latest state land tender attracts bullish top bids for 99-year private residential parcels near Kembangan and Simei MRT Stations -- indicating developers now willing to pay even more for such sites, say market watchers.
- About half a million taxpayers will benefit from 10 percent special rebate announced in budget fortnight ago, and will start receiving updated assessments from Monday.
- Singapore dollar has weakened against currencies of seven of its top 10 trading partners, a trend which could make its exports more competitive.
- Listed construction and property firm Koh Brothers Group says its soon-to-be-listed subsidiary G&W Group Ltd intends to offer 27 million new shares, representing 25 percent of enlarged company.
- Creative Technology turnaround underscored as its shares blasted past historical high of Singapore $36 on expectations of strong fourth-quarter results due Monday.
- Singapore Tourist Promotion Board reviewing 10 percent service charge levied by almost all hotels, restaurants and pubs.

- QAF Ltd purchase of controlling stake in Indofood Sukses Makmur is "sensitive" issue and government needs to study it before taking position, says Hartarto, Indonesia's Coordinating Minister for Production and Distribution.

- Singapore dollar falls to 33-month low of 1.4780 to U.S. dollar as European markets open on Thursday, bringing its easing against the greenback to 3.4 percent this month and 5.7 percent from 1.3980 high early this year.
- Sembawang Corp makes preliminary agreement with homegrown Vista Healthcare to set up regional healthcare investment fund here, sources say.
- Property and hotel group Amara Holdings receives in-principle approval to list on Sesdaq.
- Indonesian-linked stocks, especially those in which businessman Johannes Kotjo owns substantial stakes, make spectacular gains in market on myriad of rumours.
- Sesdaq-listed Teledata will soon join former second board counters Electronic Resources and Venture Manufacturing on the mainboard.
